newsitem.title: UK: UK to extend programme for long-term jobless.
newsitem.headline: UK to extend programme for long-term jobless.

text.p: The British government is to extend a scheme designed to help the long-term unemployed back into work, Education and Employment Secretary Gillian Shephard said on Thursday.
Under the scheme, which has been piloted in three towns, people who have been without jobs for more than two years are given three months of intensive help in searching for jobs.
Those who fail to find work are then required to take a work experience place for three months on pain of losing their unemployment benefit.
"These schemes make sense. They are working. And this afternoon I am announcing their extension to include up to 100,000 people in every region of the country," Shephard told the conference.

She said that in the three pilot areas -- Hull, Medway and Maidstone -- the number of people leaving the jobless register was more than 20 percent higher than in comparable places elsewhere in the country.
